h2: Explore every Portable Shop Cabin size & its applications
intro: Nine standard sizes, one retail specification — pick the footprint that matches how you'll trade, with fixed base prices and delivery in 7 working days.

panels.paragraph: The 10×10 ft is the compact way to open a shop: 100 sq ft with one shopfront, a roller shutter and a sliding display window, and room for one operator behind a service counter. It arrives retail-fitted and trades from day one — and when the pitch changes, the whole shop lifts and moves with you.

A narrow 160 sq ft unit that fits where wider cabins cannot — a full-length shopfront with shutter and display window on a slim body that still travels on a standard 20 ft trailer. Right for a service counter or a compact outlet on a tight frontage.

Our most-ordered shop cabin: 200 sq ft with a proper shopfront, counter and display, room for one to two operators and back-of-counter stock. It is the size most retailers specify first — delivered trading-ready and relocated as one unit when the location changes.

Two extra feet of depth turn the everyday shop into a shop-with-storage: the same shopfront and counter up front, with real stock shelving behind. 240 sq ft that keeps fast-moving inventory inside the shop instead of in a separate store.

A long 300 sq ft retail floor for a bigger outlet or a clean counter-plus-storeroom split. The extended frontage takes a wider display and a serving line, while the rear holds stock — still one relocatable unit that moves on a 40 ft trailer.

The longest slim format: 320 sq ft of continuous frontage for an arcade-style counter or an extended display run. Where footfall passes along a line — markets, complexes, transit routes — this shape puts the most shopfront in front of it.

A near-square 400 sq ft floor with a wide shopfront — space for a broad display, a serving counter and open customer standing room, or a clean shop-plus-store division. Engineered to stay liftable and reusable despite the wider body.

The full-length standard: 400 sq ft with a long shopfront, generous display and serious stock capacity. It runs as a complete retail floor — counter, display and back-of-shop — and still travels as one unit on a 40 ft open trailer.

The most retail floor you can lift and reuse as one cabin: 480 sq ft with a broad shopfront, full display run, serving counter and a real back store. For retailers who want a permanent-feeling shop that still relocates when the business moves.
